issues.title: Refine rule-aware group standings for a selected competition
issues.body:
## Problem

The requirements analysis in #183 found that the reference's group tie-break order differs from the DBV Spielordnung 2026/27 Anlage IV Teil 2 § 10. Existing `TieBreakRules` describes flags but does not establish a complete ordered standings calculation. A competition and applicable rule version must be selected before implementation. See also #185 for overlapping draw and group-rule research.

## Scope

Analysis and specification only: identify a target competition and responsible authority; verify the exact rule edition and its applicability; define input results, group completion, ties, lot outcomes, withdrawal and correction examples; and resolve the proposed ownership of results and standings across existing contexts. Reuse the research in #185 rather than duplicating it. Trace the proposed contract to STANDINGS-001 and STANDINGS-002 in the `requirements-reconciliation` OpenSpec change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The selected competition, applicable primary source, edition and scope are documented; unresolved or conflicting rules are clearly identified.
- [ ] Reviewable examples cover selected and unsupported rule versions, equal match wins, incomplete results, unresolved ties, and withdrawal or correction where applicable.
- [ ] Proposed bounded-context ownership and prerequisites are documented, including any potential migration, module, public API or compatibility impact.
- [ ] Existing #185 research is referenced and overlapping work is reconciled.
- [ ] The resulting specification and decisions are independently reviewed; no production code, tests, migration, runtime configuration or dependency files are changed.

## Validation

Run `npm run format:check`; check any new untracked Markdown explicitly with Prettier; validate any OpenSpec change with the repository-pinned OpenSpec 1.14.2 CLI. Verify rule examples against the named primary sources.

This follow-up does not authorize implementation or assume that the DBV example applies to every RallyOn event.
